selection: 11 primary papers/specifications/docs covering compute denomination, delivery, incentives and payment; not an exhaustive crawl

sources.title: Bootstrapping a stable computation token
sources.locator: Sections 2–4; CPU task pricing and TRU conversion
sources.text: The proposal prices Truebit computation steps in CPU tokens and rewards solvers/verifiers in TRU, using bonded local prices for conversion.
sources.limitation: A proposed incentive model is not proof of reserved future GPU capacity or arbitrary LLM quality.

sources.title: ClawCoin: An Agentic AI-Native Cryptocurrency for Decentralized Agent Economies
sources.text: The proposal links token NAV to a versioned AI API cost basket and uses fiat-backed collateral such as USDC. It reports a prototype and simulations.
sources.limitation: The claim is index-linked financial value, not direct physical compute redemption; results were not independently reproduced here.

sources.title: Cycle costs
sources.locator: Cycle denomination and resource cost tables
sources.text: ICP cycles pay resource charges; one trillion cycles is pegged to one XDR.
sources.limitation: XDR is the anchor, not a fixed physical compute unit. Tables and web documentation can change.

sources.title: What Burn-Mint Equilibrium Means for Akash
sources.locator: BME Tokenomics Overview; Vault and Circuit Breakers; Testnet Observations
sources.text: The described model burns AKT for non-transferable USD-pegged ACT compute credits and settles provider payments through burn/mint accounting.
sources.limitation: The article's testnet observations do not establish independently verified current mainnet readiness or guaranteed stabilization.

sources.title: The RENDER SPL Token
sources.text: RENDER is burned for USD-equivalent non-transferable work credits; nodes receive token emissions under the network's proposals.
sources.limitation: Work credits are dollar-valued; this is not a fixed-quantity compute peg.

sources.title: Payments in Golem explained
sources.locator: Introduction; Pay as you go; Keep-alive; Mid-agreement payments
sources.text: Providers quote resource prices, usage is invoiced in GLM, and negotiated interim payments limit unpaid work exposure.
sources.limitation: Using a token to pay for computation does not fix its resource purchasing power; provider metering needs separate trust analysis.

sources.title: Filecoin: A Decentralized Storage Network
sources.text: The paper defines proof-of-replication and proof-of-spacetime for storage commitments and describes storage/retrieval markets.
sources.limitation: Storage-specific proofs do not certify arbitrary GPU computation, LLM answers or future service availability; this historical paper is not a current protocol audit.

sources.title: dTAO Whitepaper
sources.text: The paper describes subnet AMMs, TAO/alpha exchange, incentive emissions and a simplified economic model.
sources.limitation: Subnet prices and incentive scores do not establish a fixed quantity of redeemable compute. No current emission ratios are adopted.

sources.title: MLPerf Inference 5.1: Benchmarking Small LLMs with Llama3.1-8B
sources.locator: Latency constraints for server and interactive scenarios; metrics
sources.text: The benchmark separates workload scenarios and measures tokens per second with explicit first-token and per-output-token latency constraints.
sources.limitation: A benchmark constrains a workload, not universal intelligence; no MLPerf benchmark was run for this prototype.

sources.title: ERC-1155: Multi Token Standard
sources.text: The standard identifies token types by IDs and supports multiple fungible and non-fungible token types in one contract.
sources.limitation: It can represent distinct service series, but supplies no physical backing, expiry policy, verifier or peg. No chain or contract has been selected.

sources.title: x402 Specification v2
sources.revision: x402 v2; main branch observed without commit pin
sources.text: Payment requirements distinguish scheme, network, amount, asset, recipient and timeout for HTTP payments.
sources.limitation: Payment transport does not define compute units or prove delivery; asset and scheme support require implementation and testing.
